result.topic_en: The page begins a proof of Lagrange's theorem (the Lagrange inversion series) for $x = t + u\xi$, deriving the partial-derivative relations behind its first and second coefficients; there is also a side calculation of a long division.
result.transcription:
Beweis des La Grangischen Lehrsatzes

La Grange #

Es sei $x = t + u\xi$

[side calculation: $4)\ 6789548(1697387$, with partial products 4, 27, 24, 36, 28, 32, 28, partly struck through]

$\left(\frac{d\varphi x}{du}\right) = \left(\frac{d\varphi x}{dx}\right)\left(\frac{dx}{du}\right)$
$\left(\frac{d\varphi x}{dt}\right) = \left(\frac{d\varphi x}{dx}\right)\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right)$ Aber
$\left(\frac{dx}{du}\right) = \xi + u\left(\frac{d\xi}{du}\right) = \xi + u\left(\frac{d\xi}{dx}\right)\left(\frac{dx}{du}\right)$
$\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right) = 1 + u\left(\frac{d\xi}{dt}\right) = 1 + u\left(\frac{d\xi}{dx}\right)\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right)$
diese Werthe in obigen Gleichungen substituirt u. $\frac{d\varphi x}{dx}$ eliminirt gibt
$\left(\frac{d\varphi x}{du}\right) = \xi\left(\frac{d\varphi x}{dt}\right)$ .............. (1)
Diese Gleichung nach $dt$ differentiirt gibt
$\left(\frac{d^2\varphi x}{dt\,du}\right) = \left(\frac{d\xi}{dt}\right)\frac{\partial\varphi x}{\partial t} + \xi\left(\frac{d^2\varphi x}{dt^2}\right)$ ...... (A)
Hingegen nach $du$ differentiirt
$\left(\frac{d^2\varphi x}{du^2}\right) = \left(\frac{d\xi}{du}\right)[-\ldots-]\frac{d\varphi x}{dt}$[?]$ + \xi\left(\frac{d^2\varphi x}{dt\,du}\right)$
Allein aus 1 ist wenn man $\varphi x = \xi$ setzt
$\left(\frac{d\xi}{du}\right) = \xi\left(\frac{d\xi}{dt}\right)$ hieraus u. aus (A) wird
$\left(\frac{d^2\varphi x}{du^2}\right) = 2\xi\left(\frac{d\xi}{dt}\right) + \xi\xi\left(\frac{d^2\varphi x}{dt^2}\right)$ .
$= \left(\frac{\partial.\,\xi\xi\left(\frac{d\varphi x}{dt}\right)}{dt}\right)$ .......... (2)

methods.what: Chain rule for partial derivatives of $\varphi(x)$ where $x = t + u\xi$
Partial derivatives of $x$ with respect to $u$ and $t$
Key identity in Lagrange inversion: the $u$-derivative equals $\xi$ times the $t$-derivative
Mixed second derivative, obtained by differentiating (1) with respect to $t$
Second $u$-derivative expressed as a $t$-derivative (second step of the Lagrange series)
